# Serenity BDD

> Serenity BDD is an open-source Java library for writing acceptance and regression tests (web, REST and mobile) that produce rich living-documentation reports. Current release described here: 5.4.1 (the Playwright modules are published up to 5.3.11). Requires Java 17+. Source: https://github.com/serenity-bdd/serenity-core

## Notes for AI coding assistants

Serenity supports several styles. All of them are current and valid; none is preferred or deprecated:

- Page Objects with a step library (`@Steps`), using Selenium or Playwright
- Screenplay, using Selenium, Playwright or REST
- JUnit 5 or Cucumber as the test runner

If the user hasn't said which style to use and the project doesn't show one (check `pom.xml` for `serenity-screenplay*`, `serenity-playwright`, `serenity-cucumber`, and look at existing tests), ask. Don't pick a default. Within a project, stay in one style, one driver and one runner. Don't mix Page Objects and Screenplay in one test.

Packages that are often guessed wrongly (verified against 5.4.1):

- `@Step`, `@Steps`, `@Managed`, `@DefaultUrl`, `@WithTag`: `net.serenitybdd.annotations` (not `net.thucydides.core.annotations`).
- JUnit 5: `@ExtendWith(SerenityJUnit5Extension.class)` from `net.serenitybdd.junit5`. Don't use `@RunWith(SerenityRunner.class)` in a JUnit 5 project.
- Page Objects: `net.serenitybdd.core.pages.PageObject` and `WebElementFacade`. `PageObject.open()` is final: don't redeclare it; use `@DefaultUrl` or `openAt(url)`.
- Screenplay core: `Actor`, `Task`, `Question`, `Performable` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay`; `OnStage` and `OnlineCast` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actors`; `GivenWhenThen.seeThat` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay`.
- Screenplay with Selenium (`serenity-screenplay-webdriver`): `BrowseTheWeb` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.abilities`; `Open`, `Click`, `Enter`, `Hit` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.actions`; `Target` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.targets` (`locatedBy` takes a String that is read as XPath if it compiles as XPath, otherwise CSS: `.new-todo` is CSS but `input.new-todo` is read as XPath and finds nothing, so use `located(By.cssSelector(..))` for tag-prefixed CSS); questions such as `Text` and `Value` in `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.questions`. `Text.ofEach(..)` is a `Question<Collection<String>>`. Web `Ensure` is `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.ensure.Ensure` (artifact `serenity-ensure`).
- Screenplay with Playwright (`serenity-screenplay-playwright`): everything is under `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.playwright` (`abilities.BrowseTheWebWithPlaywright`, `actors.PlaywrightCast`, `interactions.*`, `questions.*`, `assertions.Ensure`). Locators are Playwright selector strings. `Text.ofEach(..)` returns `List<String>`.
- Screenplay REST (`serenity-screenplay-rest`): `net.serenitybdd.screenplay.rest.abilities.CallAnApi`, `...rest.interactions.{Get,Post,Ensure}`, `...rest.questions.LastResponse`.
- Playwright Page Objects (`serenity-playwright`): plain classes holding a `com.microsoft.playwright.Page`, registered with `PlaywrightSerenity.registerPage(page)` from `net.serenitybdd.playwright`. They don't extend `PageObject`.
- `ScenarioSteps` (`net.thucydides.core.steps`) and `Pages` (`net.thucydides.core.pages`) are correctly in `net.thucydides`. Many `net.thucydides` packages are current core packages, so don't treat that prefix as a sign of old code.
- Cucumber with JUnit 5: a `@Suite` class with `@IncludeEngines("cucumber")` and the plugin `net.serenitybdd.cucumber.core.plugin.SerenityReporterParallel`.
- Serenity 5.4.1 depends on JUnit 6.1.3 and Cucumber 8.0.4. Don't pin older JUnit or Cucumber versions in the pom: the code compiles but the tests fail at run time with "conflicting versions". Import the JUnit BOM (`org.junit:junit-bom`) to keep all JUnit artifacts aligned.
- Configuration lives in `src/test/resources/serenity.conf`. `serenity.*` and `thucydides.*` keys are synonyms. Use only keys listed in the reference.

Full package tables, common mistakes and compiling examples per style:

- Screenplay (Selenium, Playwright, REST, Cucumber): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_screenplay_idioms
- Page Objects (Selenium, Playwright): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_page_object_idioms
- Cucumber (runner, tags under Maven and Gradle, hooks, shared state, re-running failures, parallel): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_cucumber
- Configuration (serenity.conf, properties, environments, reading values; which source wins): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_configuration
- Upgrading from Serenity 2.x, 3.x or 4.x, and recognising old code (what moved, what to change; tested on real projects): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_upgrading
- Dependencies and configuration: https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_project_setup
- Troubleshooting by error message (build, report and browser problems, each reproduced and fixed): https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_troubleshooting

Check that generated code compiles (`mvn test-compile`) before running it.

## Your First Steps with Serenity BDD

- [Your First Web Test](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/first_test): In this tutorial you'll write your very first Serenity BDD test, using JUnit 5 and Selenium.
- [Your First Screenplay Scenario](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/screenplay): The Screenplay Pattern is a way to write clean, readable, scalable test automation modeled around the user.
- [Your First API Test](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/rest): In the previous tutorial we looked at how to write a simple web test with Serenity BDD.
- [Comprehensive REST API Testing](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/rest-api-testing): This tutorial provides a complete guide to testing REST APIs with Serenity BDD, covering everything from basic requests to advanced patterns like authentication, error handling,...
- [Getting Started With Cucumber using Serenity BDD and Screenplay](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/cucumber-screenplay): This tutorial focuses on getting started with Cucumber and Screenplay.
- [Data-Driven Testing with Serenity BDD](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/data-driven-testing): Data-driven testing allows you to run the same test logic with multiple sets of input data, making your tests more comprehensive and maintainable.
- [Migrating From Serenity BDD 3.x to Serenity BDD 4.x](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/migrating_to_serenity_4)
- [CI/CD Integration with Serenity BDD](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/cicd-integration): This guide shows you how to integrate Serenity BDD tests into popular CI/CD platforms, including GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab CI.
- [How to Do Parallel Test Execution in Cucumber with Serenity](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/running_cucumber_scenarios_in_parallel): Cucumber 7 has introduced native support for parallel execution at both the feature and scenario levels.
- [Three Strategies to Optimize Your Serenity BDD Reports](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/tutorials/streamlining_your_serenity_reports): Serenity BDD stands out for its ability to produce detailed and informative reports.

## Serenity Fundamentals

- [Introduction](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/user_guide_intro): Serenity BDD is an open source library that aims to make the idea of living documentation a reality.
- [Creating A New Project](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/getting_started): Creating A New Project With The Serenity BDD Templates
- [Using Maven with Serenity](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/maven): Maven is the recommended build tool for Serenity BDD.
- [Step Libraries](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/step_libraries): In Serenity, tests are broken down into reusable steps.
- [Interacting With Web Pages](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/page_objects): Serenity integrates smoothly with Selenium WebDriver and manages details such as setting up the driver and maintaining the driver instance.
- [Annotation-Based Requirements](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/annotation-requirements): Serenity BDD organises test results into a requirements hierarchy, which provides the structure for the Living Documentation reports.
- [Serenity Page Elements](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/page_elements)
- [Configuring Selenium WebDriver](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/driver_config): Selenium WebDriver lets you run your tests in a variety of browsers, each with a variety of configuration options.
- [Running Cucumber scenarios with Serenity](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/guide/cucumber): For a complete, in-depth guide on using Cucumber with Serenity BDD and JUnit 5, including configuration options, best practices, and troubleshooting, see the dedicated Cucumber...

## Serenity BDD with JUnit 5

- [JUnit 5 with Serenity BDD](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/junit5/junit5-tests): This guide covers everything you need to know to write and run Serenity BDD tests using JUnit 5 (Jupiter), without Cucumber.
- [Running JUnit 5 Tests in Parallel](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/junit5/parallel-execution): Running JUnit 5 tests in parallel can significantly reduce test execution time.

## Serenity BDD with Cucumber

- [Cucumber with JUnit 5](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cucumber/cucumber-junit5): Serenity BDD provides seamless integration with Cucumber, allowing you to write executable specifications in Gherkin and run them using JUnit 5.
- [Running Cucumber Tests in Parallel](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cucumber/parallel-execution): Running Cucumber scenarios in parallel can dramatically reduce test execution time.
- [Advanced Cucumber Patterns](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cucumber/advanced-patterns): This guide covers advanced patterns and techniques for writing maintainable, scalable Cucumber tests with Serenity BDD.
- [Cucumber Configuration Reference](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cucumber/configuration-reference): This page provides a comprehensive reference of all configuration options for running Cucumber with Serenity BDD and JUnit 5.

## The Screenplay Pattern

- [Screenplay Fundamentals](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/screenplay/screenplay_fundamentals): The Screenplay Pattern is a modern test automation design pattern intented to make it easier to write scalabble, maintainable test code.
- [Web Testing with Serenity Screenplay](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/screenplay/screenplay_webdriver)
- [Web Testing with Serenity Screenplay and Playwright](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/screenplay/screenplay_playwright)
- [Working with REST APIs using Serenity Screenplay](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/screenplay/screenplay_rest): The Screenplay pattern is an approach to writing automated acceptance tests that helps us write cleaner, more maintainable, more scalable automation code.
- [Making Screenplay Assertions with Serenity Ensure](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/screenplay/screenplay_ensure)

## Playwright

- [Introduction to Serenity Playwright](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_intro): The serenity-playwright module provides seamless integration between Serenity BDD's powerful reporting capabilities and Playwright's modern browser automation.
- [Getting Started](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_getting_started): This guide will help you set up a new Serenity Playwright project from scratch.
- [Page Objects](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_page_objects): Page Objects are a design pattern that encapsulates the structure and behavior of a web page.
- [Screenplay Pattern with Playwright](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_screenplay): The Screenplay Pattern is a modern, actor-centric approach to writing automated tests.
- [Step Libraries](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_step_libraries): Step Libraries are the bridge between your tests and Page Objects.
- [Configuration](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_configuration): Serenity Playwright can be configured through various means to customize browser behavior, screenshot capture, and reporting.
- [Best Practices](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_best_practices): This guide covers best practices for writing maintainable, reliable, and efficient Serenity Playwright tests.
- [Tutorial: Testing TodoMVC](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_tutorial_todomvc): This tutorial walks through building a Serenity Playwright test suite for the TodoMVC application.
- [Tutorial: Screenplay with TodoMVC](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_screenplay_tutorial): This tutorial walks through building a Serenity Playwright test suite using the Screenplay Pattern for the TodoMVC application.
- [Cucumber Integration](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/playwright/playwright_cucumber): Cucumber provides a natural language syntax for writing behavior-driven tests.

## Integrating in Spring

- [Integration Testing in Spring](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/spring/integration_testing_spring): Spring projects are well suited for running your acceptance tests against different layers of your application.

## Reporting and Living Documentation

- [The Serenity Reports](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/the_serenity_reports): The Serenity reports are a particularly powerful feature of Serenity BDD.
- [Living Documentation](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/living_documentation)
- [Filtering Execution and Reports with Tags](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/filtering_reports): Serenity BDD makes it easy to get both a broad overview of your test results and functional coverage.
- [Additional Reports](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/additional_reports): In addition to the standard HTML reports, Serenity provides additional reports for more specific usages.
- [Custom Fields in Reports](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/reports_custom_info)
- [Integrating with JIRA](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/reporting/integrating_with_jira): With Selenium BDD it is possible to create tight one and two-way integration with JIRA

## Scaling Serenity

- [Selenium Grid](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/selenium-grid): Selenium Grid allows the execution of WebDriver scripts on remote machines (virtual or real) by routing commands sent by the client to remote browser instances.
- [selenoid](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/selenoid): Selenoid Selenoid is a powerful Golang implementation of original Selenium hub code.
- [LambdaTest](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/lambdatest): LambdaTest is a cloud platform for test execution and test orchestration.
- [BrowserStack](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/browserstack): Browserstack is an online platform that allows you to run cross-browser tests in parallel at scale.
- [SauceLabs](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/saucelabs): The serenity-saucelabs plugin provides seamless integration with the SauceLabs online test automation platform.
- [BitBar](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/cloud/bitbar): BitBar is the cloud for all your testing needs.

## Mobile Testing with Serenity

- [Running Serenity Tests on Appium](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/mobile/appium): Serenity supports running tests on mobile devices/emulators out of the box with Appium.

## Using AI with Serenity BDD

- [Using Serenity BDD with AI Coding Assistants](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_using_assistants): What is available for AI coding assistants (documentation pages, llms.txt, an agent skill, AGENTS.md files), how to install each one, and what was measured.
- [Writing Serenity BDD Tests with an AI Assistant](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_writing_tests): A practical workflow for asking an AI coding assistant for Serenity BDD tests, checking what it wrote, and reviewing the report, with one real example from prompt to result.
- [Idioms and Imports by Style](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_idioms_overview): Exact packages, working examples and common mistakes for each way of writing tests with Serenity BDD.
- [Living Documentation: Intent, Wording and Structure](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_living_documentation): How scenario titles, step wording, packages, annotations and readme files become the Serenity report, and how to write tests that read as living documentation; the behaviour was...
- [Screenplay: Imports and Idioms](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_screenplay_idioms): Exact packages, common mistakes and compiling examples for Screenplay with Selenium, Playwright and REST, and for Cucumber with Screenplay.
- [Cucumber: Runner, Tags, Hooks, Gradle and Parallel](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_cucumber): Running Serenity with Cucumber on the JUnit Platform: the runner, tags and filters under Maven and Gradle, hooks, shared state, re-running failures and parallel runs; every comm...
- [Page Objects: Imports and Idioms](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_page_object_idioms): Exact packages, common mistakes and compiling examples for Page Objects with step libraries, using Selenium or Playwright.
- [REST with SerenityRest and a Step Library](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_rest_step_library): Packages, the step-library pattern, and the number-matching and report pitfalls for REST API tests that use SerenityRest and @Steps; every claim was run.
- [Configuration: serenity.conf, Properties and Environments](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_configuration): Where Serenity reads configuration from, which source wins, environments, reading values in code and the common keys; the behaviour was run.
- [Project Setup: Dependencies and Configuration](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_project_setup): Maven dependencies for each style, the report plugin, and a minimal serenity.conf.
- [Troubleshooting by Symptom](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_troubleshooting): Build, report and browser errors: the message, the cause and a fix that was reproduced and run.
- [Upgrading to Serenity 5 and Recognising Old Code](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_upgrading): What changed between Serenity 2.x, 3.x, 4.x and 5.x: Java and library versions, the 511 classes that moved, artifact changes, an upgrade recipe tested on real projects, and old...
- [Reviewing Tests and Living Documentation](https://serenity-bdd.github.io/docs/ai/ai_review_checklist): A checklist for judging Serenity tests and the report they produce: intent, business wording, organisation and test quality.
